facts.text: Seaport District's Commonwealth Pier was built in 1901 as the world's largest pier, handling freight and passenger traffic with rail and truck access.
In 1986, the Massachusetts Port Authority turned Commonwealth Pier into the World Trade Center Boston, a modern hub for commerce and events.
The Seaport District hosts the Institute of Contemporary Art, a museum that showcases daring exhibitions and pushes artistic boundaries.
Seaport Hotel and World Trade Center earned Forbes Traveler's 2008 title of "America's Greenest Hotels" and runs a certified green restaurant.
The Seaport District's history dates back to 1630 when Boston Harbor first opened, making it a cradle of early American maritime trade.
The Silver Line's World Trade Center station connects the Seaport District directly to downtown Boston, making it a key public‑transport link.
